title: New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District pits four-term Republican incumbent Jeff Van Drew against Democratic nominee Zack Mullock, the two-term mayor of Cape May. The district covers Atlantic, Cape May, Cumberland, and Salem counties, plus parts of Gloucester and Ocean counties, and has a slight Republican voter registration edge. Van Drew, who was originally elected as a Democrat in 2018 before switching parties in 2019, is running on a platform of energy independence, border security, and deregulation. Mullock, who won a competitive four-way Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, is campaigning on affordability, healthcare access, and coastal resilience, with Democrats viewing this as their best opportunity in years to flip the seat amid low approval ratings for President Donald Trump, a key Van Drew ally.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically matching the Van Drew vs. Mullock general election matchup in New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District for 2026. A reference to a Democratic group conducting internal polling in NJ-02 was identified but no specific numbers were publicly available.

candidates.name: Jeff Van Drew
candidates.summary: Jeff Van Drew is the four-term Republican incumbent representing New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District. First elected as a Democrat in 2018, he switched to the Republican Party in December 2019 and has since become a strong ally of President Donald Trump. Van Drew previously served three terms in the New Jersey General Assembly and four terms in the New Jersey State Senate, and practiced dentistry for 30 years before entering politics. His campaign focuses on energy independence, border security, reducing federal regulation, and what he describes as delivering results for South Jersey, including funding for coastal protection and infrastructure.

candidates.name: Zack Mullock
candidates.summary: Zack Mullock is the Democratic nominee for New Jersey's 2nd Congressional District and the two-term Mayor of Cape May, a position he has held since 2021. Born and raised in South Jersey, Mullock holds a BA from Mount Saint Mary's University and an MBA in Finance from Saint Joseph's University, and previously worked as a PGA golf professional and managed historic properties in Cape May. His campaign emphasizes affordability, healthcare access, coastal resilience, and small-business growth, highlighting his record of not raising taxes as mayor while delivering infrastructure improvements, a new firehouse and library, and increased public safety staffing.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for this matchup (only a reference to internal Democratic polling with no released numbers). With zero numeric polling data, the forecast relies on race fundamentals. Van Drew is a four-term incumbent with a slight Republican voter registration edge in the district, making him a narrow favorite. However, he is a party-switcher (elected as a Democrat in 2018, switched in 2019), which may complicate his coalition. Democratic nominee Zack Mullock is a credible challenger—two-term mayor of Cape May with executive experience—and won a competitive four-way primary on June 2, 2026, suggesting Democratic enthusiasm. The race is described as Democrats' best flip opportunity in years, with low Trump approval ratings cited as a potential headwind for Van Drew, a close Trump ally. The combination of incumbent advantage and registration edge vs. a credible challenger and unfavorable national environment suggests a narrow Republican edge, but the absence of polling makes this highly uncertain.
